accepted.s: Under the Zamindari system in the Northern Circars, the revenue settlement was made directly with whom?
accepted.x: Under the Zamindari or Permanent Settlement system, the Company made the revenue settlement with the zamindar, who acted as an intermediary between the government and the cultivators.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the person with whom the settlement was directly made.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the revenue systems in the Andhra region:
1. Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were estates under the Zamindari system.
2. Ryotwari settlement was made directly with the cultivator.
3. Mahalwari settlement was associated with village headmen collecting revenue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Zamindari applied to estates such as Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram; Ryotwari dealt directly with the ryot; and Mahalwari involved collection through village headmen.
accepted.tq: Test a comparison table by separating the settlement unit and collecting agency.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes an important effect of the Zamindari system in the Northern Circars?
o: Uniform assessment limited to one-fourth of the produce
Transfer of all land rights to village headmen
Absentee landlordism and impoverishment of tenants
accepted.x: The Zamindari system encouraged absentee landlordism and contributed to the impoverishment of tenants.
accepted.tq: Identify the consequence rather than the formal structure of the system.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s: Which of the following was a major consequence associated with the Ryotwari system in the Andhra region?
o: Abolition of direct contact between cultivator and government
Over-assessment, indebtedness to moneylenders and land alienation
Fixed revenue payable only by zamindars
accepted.x: Ryotwari areas experienced heavy assessment, often exceeding 50 percent of the produce, along with dependence on moneylenders and alienation of land.
accepted.tq: Link the revenue arrangement with its stated economic consequences.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s: Mahalwari settlement, in the classification used for the Andhra region, was associated with which area?
accepted.x: The Mahalwari system, under which village headmen collected revenue, is placed in Nellore in the stated classification.
accepted.tq: Use location-based discrimination among neighbouring revenue systems.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s: The first region where the Ryotwari system was introduced was:
accepted.x: Ryotwari was first introduced in Baramahal in 1792, the area now comprising Salem and Krishnagiri in Tamil Nadu, under Captain Alexander Read with Munro.
accepted.tq: Separate the first introduction from the later introduction in Andhra.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s: In Andhra, the Ryotwari system began first in the Ceded Districts in:
accepted.x: Although Ryotwari began in Baramahal in 1792, its introduction in Andhra started in the Ceded Districts in 1802.
accepted.tq: Compare a general starting date with the date of regional introduction.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s: The Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948 came into force on:
accepted.x: The 1948 Act abolishing the Zamindari system came into force on 7 September 1949.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of an Act from the date on which it came into force.
accepted.sec: Revenue system - Permanent Settlement areas vs Ryotwari areas

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the territories included in the Ceded Districts in 1800?
accepted.x: The Ceded Districts comprised Kadapa, Kurnool and Anantapur in present-day Andhra Pradesh, together with Bellary, now in Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Check membership in a historically defined regional group.
accepted.sec: Ceded Districts - region, old name, Rayalaseema, headquarters

accepted.s: The old name used for the Ceded Districts was:
accepted.x: The region was known as Dattamandalam or Dattamandalalu, meaning the ceded lands, until 1928.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the old regional name and the later political name.
accepted.sec: Ceded Districts - region, old name, Rayalaseema, headquarters

accepted.s: The name ‘Rayalaseema’ was adopted at the Andhra Mahasabha held at Nandyal in:
accepted.x: The name Rayalaseema was adopted at Nandyal in 1928. The meeting was presided over by S. Radhakrishnan.
accepted.tq: Test the year and venue together rather than the name alone.
accepted.sec: Ceded Districts - region, old name, Rayalaseema, headquarters

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ceded Districts:
1. Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan had taken these territories from Hyderabad.
2. Nizam Ali regained them as a British ally during the Mysore wars.
3. The Nizam ceded them in 1800 because he could not pay the Subsidiary Alliance subsidy in cash.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The territories changed hands during the Mysore conflicts and were finally ceded by the Nizam in 1800 under the Subsidiary Alliance arrangement.
accepted.tq: Trace a territorial change through successive political causes.
accepted.sec: Ceded Districts - region, old name, Rayalaseema, headquarters

accepted.s: Before the 1808 division, the single Ceded collectorate was centred at:
accepted.x: The Ceded region functioned as one collectorate centred at Anantapur under Munro until 1808. Bellary became the seat of one of the two districts after the split.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original headquarters from the later headquarters after reorganisation.
accepted.sec: Ceded Districts - region, old name, Rayalaseema, headquarters

accepted.s: Who became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800?
accepted.x: Thomas Munro became the first Collector of the Ceded Districts in 1800, with sub-collectors stationed at Harpanahalli, Kadapa, Adoni and Kurnool.
accepted.tq: Identify the official associated with the first administrative appointment.
accepted.sec: Company officials - Munro, Cotton and his assistant, C.P. Brown

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Thomas Munro — Introduced Ryotwari and surveyed the districts from 1802 to 1807
C.P. Brown — Built the Dowleswaram anicut
George Russell — Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827
accepted.x: Munro introduced Ryotwari and surveyed the Ceded Districts during 1802–07. Arthur Cotton was the irrigation engineer, C.P. Brown was the Telugu scholar, and Munro—not George Russell—was Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827.
accepted.tq: Catch the swapped official-and-work trap.
accepted.sec: Company officials - Munro, Cotton and his assistant, C.P. Brown

accepted.s: Thomas Munro served as Governor of Madras during:
accepted.x: Thomas Munro was Governor of Madras from 1820 to 1827.
accepted.tq: Use the official’s career dates to distinguish administrative posts.
accepted.sec: Company officials - Munro, Cotton and his assistant, C.P. Brown

accepted.s: Thomas Munro died at Pattikonda in Kurnool on:
accepted.x: Thomas Munro died at Pattikonda in Kurnool on 6 July 1827.
accepted.tq: Test a precise date-place association.
accepted.sec: Company officials - Munro, Cotton and his assistant, C.P. Brown

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Veenam Veeranna — Andhra assistant to Arthur Cotton
accepted.x: The Dowleswaram anicut was built across the Godavari. Arthur Cotton built the Krishna anicut at Vijayawada, and Veenam Veeranna served as his Andhra assistant.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed river-location association.
accepted.sec: Company officials - Munro, Cotton and his assistant, C.P. Brown

accepted.s: Which work is associated with C.P. Brown?
o: The construction of the Krishna anicut
Publication of Vemana’s verses and a Telugu-English dictionary
A survey of the Ceded Districts from 1802 to 1807
Suppression of the palegars of Rayalaseema
accepted.x: C.P. Brown studied Telugu thoroughly and published Vemana’s verses as well as a Telugu-English dictionary.
accepted.tq: Match the scholar with his literary contribution.
accepted.sec: Company officials - Munro, Cotton and his assistant, C.P. Brown

accepted.s: The Battle of Padmanabham was fought in:
accepted.x: The Battle of Padmanabham took place on 10 July 1794.
accepted.tq: Differentiate a close historical date from the date of the Bobbili battle.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: What was the immediate consequence of the Battle of Padmanabham for the Vizianagaram estate?
o: Bobbili Ranga Rao was appointed zamindar
Narayana Babu, the minor son, was made zamindar
The estate was transferred to Pithapuram
accepted.x: After the British defeated and killed Chinna Vijayaramaraju at Padmanabham, his minor son Narayana Babu was made zamindar.
accepted.tq: Link a battle with its succession consequence.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: Who took charge of the forts of Vizianagaram after Narayana Babu was made zamindar?
accepted.x: George Russell took charge of the forts of Vizianagaram after the minor Narayana Babu became zamindar.
accepted.tq: Identify the official connected with post-battle administration.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its historical description?
accepted.x: Vizianagaram was associated with the Pusapati family. Bobbili and Venkatagiri were associated with Velama families, while Peddapuram belonged to the Vatsavayi dynasty.
accepted.tq: Separate similar zamindari houses through family-name associations.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the zamindaris of the Northern Circars is correct?
o: The Permanent Settlement abolished fixed revenue for zamindars.
The Northern Circars had no hereditary zamindari families.
Only Venkatagiri was brought under the Permanent Settlement.
Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were pre-existing estates brought under the Permanent Settlement.
accepted.x: Vizianagaram, Bobbili and Pithapuram were pre-existing estates brought under the Permanent Settlement. The settlement made zamindars fixed-revenue holders.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement and identify the precise estate group.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: Which of the following communities formed the hereditary zamindari families of the Northern Circars?
accepted.x: The hereditary zamindari families of the Northern Circars included Velamas, Reddis and Kshatriya Rajus.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact social composition of the regional zamindari houses.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the Permanent Settlement in the Circars in 1802?
o: It introduced village headmen as the only revenue collectors.
It abolished all hereditary estates in the Northern Circars.
It made ryots the fixed-revenue holders and removed zamindars.
accepted.x: The Permanent Settlement of 1802 in the Circars made zamindars fixed-revenue holders.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the legal status created by the settlement from its later consequences.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: The hereditary zamindari of Venkatagiri was associated with which family?
accepted.x: Venkatagiri in Nellore was the zamindari of the Velugoti family.
accepted.tq: Match the estate with its ruling family.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Bobbili — British Permanent Settlement Act of 1948
accepted.x: Peddapuram was associated with the Vatsavayi dynasty. Vizianagaram was associated with the Pusapati family, while Venkatagiri belonged to the Velugoti family.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure estate-family pair and eliminate swapped associations.
accepted.sec: Zamindaris - Vizianagaram, Bobbili, Pithapuram, Venkatagiri; battles

accepted.s: During the early administration of the Northern Circars, collectors relied on which intermediaries?
accepted.x: Collectors relied on dubashis for administrative and local assistance. Munro and C.P. Brown were noted as rare Company officials who learned Telugu.
accepted.tq: Identify the local intermediary rather than the formal revenue officer.
